name: Saffron
short: In a meta-analysis of 12 depression studies, adverse effects were no more common than with placebo. In a 1-week volunteer study the higher dose lowered standing blood pressure.
text: In a meta-analysis of 12 studies in mild to moderate depression, no significant difference was detected in the incidence of adverse effects between saffron and placebo or between saffron and antidepressants. In a 1-week double-blind, placebo-controlled study in 30 healthy volunteers, the higher-dose tablet (400 mg) significantly lowered standing systolic blood pressure and mean arterial pressure. In the same study saffron slightly decreased red blood cells, haemoglobin, haematocrit and platelets and increased sodium, blood urea nitrogen and creatinine; the authors reported that these blood-test changes stayed within normal ranges and were not clinically important. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
